assembly_notes:
IDENTITY. A hand-held COMPRESSION riveter: a forged frame whose throat carries two opposed dies on one shared axis, a hand drive that closes the upper die onto the lower one, and an independently adjustable lower die that sets rivet length. It is not a blind-rivet puller — that is the explicit must_not_become sibling, and origin 003 is the pool's own negative example (see the SourceMap section 'Resolving the 003 rejection').

DOMAIN. core_domain = 5 yoke_frame x 6 squeeze_mechanism x 4 head_module x 4 return_element x 3 handle_lock = 1440. raw_domain = 1440 as well, because this category has NO multiplicity axis. Palette, continuous proportions, grip ribs and thread crest counts enter neither.

MULTIPLICITY IS EMPTY, DELIBERATELY. Every one of the 13 records has exactly TWO dies, one upper and one lower, and that count is load-bearing for the identity anchor — a single die on an outward axis is the blind riveter. There is no second lever, no second link, no turret of sets and no indexed jaw anywhere in the pool. The only index-general loops are decorative features on a single welded part: 6 grip ribs unioned into the grip solid (001 L178, L209), 2 jaw fastener studs (002 L205-L211), 7 and 8 thread crests (screw_press L352-L358, L393-L399) and 2 tommy-bar end knobs (L317-L323). Per VISUAL_DIVERSITY_MODEL decoration density does not enter core or raw, and N must not be used to inflate the domain. Declaring an N here would be inventing a mechanism the sources do not have.

ALL 1440 COMBINATIONS MUST BUILD, AND TWO DECOMPOSITION ERRORS WERE FIXED TO MAKE THAT TRUE. TemplateDomain has no compatibility gates, so a combination that cannot build is a slot boundary drawn in the wrong place. (a) `alligator_jaw` originally bundled the long upper-jaw frame WITH the swinging lower jaw that carries the lower set; that made alligator_jaw x screw_press unbuildable, because the screw press replaces the hand lever with a drive head and leaves no swinging member to carry a die. The swinging jaw is now the sixth squeeze_mechanism candidate, `direct_jaw_lever`. The source supports the split: the fork welds its set into moving_grip only because its parent 003 has no anvil part at all. (b) `quick_change_yoke_clip` was a retainer with no die, so a seed under it would have had a clip and no set; its record's own `_nosepiece_shape` (003 L52-L77) supplies the set form and is now cited alongside the clip. Both corrections are written up in the SourceMap under 'Slot-decomposition correction (phase B)'.

CROSS-SLOT RISKS, ALL RESOLVED BY DERIVATION RATHER THAN EXCLUSION.
1. Throat vs die stack vs stroke. `compact_straight_head` has the tightest throat in the pool (0.032 m clear) while `plain_die_pair` carries the tallest stack and the largest open gap (0.013 m). `throat_stroke_clearance_m` derives the margin and the frame's beam faces are placed from `upper_jaw_underside_z_m` / `lower_jaw_top_z_m`, so the throat grows with the head module instead of being a fixed silhouette number. This pair gets a named corner.
2. Drive authority vs authored stroke. `screw_press` can deliver turns x lead = 0.875 mm at the source's pi turn range, well under `plain_die_pair`'s 11 mm stroke. `ram_travel_available_m` exposes this so the mechanism widens its own turn range rather than the head module shrinking its gap. Named corner.
3. Lever length is not independent of lever travel. The category asserts BOTH a >= 25 mm grip motion and a 0.5-5.0 mm closed grip gap, so `grip_lever_arm_m` is derived from `lever_travel_rad`. `direct_jaw_lever`'s 2 deg arc therefore forces a long jaw, which is exactly what its source builds (0.190 m).
4. Mechanisms without a hand lever. `screw_press` has no handle pivot and no moving grip, so `return_spring_pivot_xyz` moves the torsion coil onto the drive-head axis (a real revolute, L287-L288) and `latch_parent_role` falls back to 003's frame-heel construction. Both are re-derivations of attested patterns, not exclusions.

ONE SOURCEMAP CLAIM CORRECTED HERE. The SourceMap said the eccentric cam's reaction bracket blocks merging the FIXED fixed_handle into the frame. On re-examination it does not: the bracket is fixed to the frame either way, so merging makes it a frame feature and the lobe-to-bracket pair stays exactly as cross-part as before. `fixed_grip_is_separate_part` is therefore 'no' for all six mechanisms — the majority construction (001, 003 and their eight forks all weld the grip into the frame) and it removes allow_overlap site 4 outright. What eccentric_cam genuinely needs is the derived bracket and bridge, encoded as the `reaction_bracket_required` gate in binding `cam_reaction_adaptation` so the adaptation is machine-visible rather than a comment.

COLLISION COUNT AND THE WELD RULE. sdk/_core/v0/exact_collisions.py:94-118 derives one collision solid per visual, 1:1. `screw_press` builds its ram from 9 visuals (screw + 7 thread crests + die) and its anvil from 13 (stem + 8 crests + 4 turnings) — 22 mutually embedded collision solids on two roughly 15 mm parts. That is legal, since it is all intra-part (MECHANICAL_PRIORS §1c), but it is the same construction that made the lighthouse category the fleet's only Genesis failure. The pool contains the better route and the rebuild uses it everywhere: `_rotating_set_holder_shape` (L220-L249) unions three turnings and cuts a socket into ONE CadQuery solid emitted as ONE visual, and `_nosepiece_shape` (003 L52-L77) does the same for shank + collar + tip - bore. Thread crests become a lathed groove in the same solid. Grip ribs are already welded in the source (001 L178-L185) and stay that way. Target: one visual per die part, one per frame, one per lever.

THE allow_overlap SITUATION — THE SINGLE BIGGEST RISK IN THIS CATEGORY. All 13 records use ctx.allow_overlap, 41 calls in total, 2 to 6 per record. Preflight BLOCKS allow_overlap for Design-backed templates and re-checks emitted allowances in the author-test report, so helper indirection will not hide it. ctx.allow_isolated_part is NOT blocked and is the sanctioned escape for joint-carried members. The SourceMap enumerates 14 distinct sites; every one reduces to three moves, and each move is encoded as a binding above rather than left to the implementation:
(a) MOVE THE PIN ONTO THE MOVING MEMBER. `pin_bore_fit.pin_owner_part` = 'squeeze_lever'. Source 001 L311-L316 puts main_pivot_pin on moving_handle and needs no allowance anywhere; 002 and 003 put every pin on the frame and pay an allowance for every pivot. Intra-part embedding is free, so the pin can sit in its own hub at zero clearance while only the host bore needs a real gap: pin_r = bore_r - 0.6 mm, host_bore_r = member_bore_r + 0.4 mm. Removes sites 5, 7, 8, 10, 14.
(b) CUT THE COUNTERBORES THE SOURCES ASSERTED BUT NEVER MACHINED. Binding `counterbore_seats` derives the anvil collar pocket (002 declared 5.0-6.5 mm of penetration instead of cutting it), the screw-register pocket (3.5 mm), the set through-bore in the jaw tip, and clamps every turned step below its guide bore via `max_die_step_r_m`. Removes sites 3, 6, 9, 11, 12, 13. Each pocket carries a 0.2 mm axial clearance because fcl.collide reports distance exactly 0 as a collision, so a coincident face is not a safe seat.
(c) allow_isolated_part FOR MEMBERS CARRIED BY THEIR JOINT — the lever, the compound link and the latch. `latch_support_mode` records this. Removes sites 1 and 2, where 001 spears its latch wire on a pin 3 mm off the hinge axis and hooks it around the fixed grip with 1.4 mm of interference. The replacement is 003's construction, the pool's only allowance-free rotary capture: a real annular eye of ID axle_r + 0.2 mm centred ON the joint origin, verified with expect_within (L546-L554).
There is no site in this pool that genuinely requires allow_overlap.

PART TREE. frame (root) -> squeeze_lever/drive_head -> [compound_link] , frame -> upper_die, frame -> lower_die (or moving_jaw carries the lower set under direct_jaw_lever), frame or lever -> handle_lock. Seeds carry 3 to 6 parts and 2 to 4 joints. Every revolute is about +-Y except the screw_press drive head, which turns about the squeeze axis — that exception is scoped into its own anchor rather than weakening the shared one.

derived.name: connection_overlap_m
derived.rationale: THE deliberate overlap for every CROSS-PART CONNECTION in this template. MECHANICAL_PRIORS §1c: two parts landing on an exact tangent face is fragile — CadQuery's union can keep tangent solids separate, triangulation can open at the seam, and find_part_geometry_connectivity_findings uses contact_tol=1e-6 (geometry_qc.py L3092), so a kiss that opens by one triangle reads as an isolated part. Magnitude 0.25 mm, the middle of the 0.1-0.3 mm band for a hand tool of this scale (frames 0.21-0.35 m, dies 3-10 mm). It is invisible to the overlap gate: find_geometry_overlaps (L1783-L1793) only calls fcl.collide when the AABB intersection depth exceeds overlap_tol on ALL THREE axes, and overlap_tol defaults to 1e-3 (L3251) with fleet templates authoring 0.002-0.006 — so 0.25 mm on a single contact normal is 4x below even the strictest default and 250x above the connectivity tolerance. It must also exceed the tessellation chord error or the seam can still open, which is what mesh_chord_tol_m below is for.

derived.name: mesh_chord_tol_m
derived.rationale: Tessellation tolerance for every mesh_from_cadquery call, tied to the overlap rather than authored separately. The pool is inconsistent here and it matters: 001 uses tolerance=0.12 and 003 tolerance=0.20 in millimetre units (unit_scale=MM) while 002 uses 0.0007 in metres — 0.7 mm, which is nearly 3x the connection overlap and would let a seam open anyway. Deriving it at 0.6x guarantees the chord error is always finer than the overlap it has to survive.

derived.name: intra_part_embed_m
derived.rationale: Weld depth between two VISUALS OF ONE PART. Collision is computed only between parts (§1c), so this is free at any depth and is used generously to guarantee the union takes. The pool already does exactly this: 001's return spring spans y -0.0098..-0.0132 against a frame face at -0.010 (0.2 mm in), 002's side_cover is 0.002 m thick at y=+0.015 against a +0.015 face (half embedded), 003's main_pivot_cap sits 0.5 mm inside its cheek. 0.5 mm is the pool's deepest and costs nothing.

derived.name: running_fit_min_m
derived.rationale: Floor for every CROSS-PART RUNNING FIT — pairs with relative motion, which must keep a real gap and must NOT be given the connection overlap. Source 001 L312 vs L150-L154: pin 0.0062 in a 0.0068 bore. Collapsing running fits into connections would jam the mechanism; collapsing connections into tangency would disconnect the part. The two are kept distinct on purpose.

derived.name: contact_class_map
derived.rationale: The taxonomy every site in this design is classified under. SAME PART (fixed grip into the frame, cam reaction bracket into the frame, quick-change clip into the frame, all three return springs, the direct_jaw_lever lower set into its jaw, the toggle cross-pin into the ram, every pivot pin into its own moving member): weld with intra_part_embed_m, free. CONNECTION (the pivot pin head lapping the frame cheek, the toggle boss lapping the ram head, the quick-change clip lapping the set collar): connection_overlap_m along ONE contact normal only, so the AABB intersection depth stays under overlap_tol on that axis and find_geometry_overlaps never calls fcl.collide on the pair. RUNNING FIT (pin in bore, ram and anvil in their guide bores, tommy bar in its head bore, latch eye on its axle, lever plate beside the frame cheek, torsion coil beside the lever, cam lobe against its reaction pin, anvil collar in its counterbore, screw register in its pocket): a real gap, never an overlap — these pairs MOVE relative to one another and an overlap would jam them at some pose in the sweep.

derived.name: joint_carried_parts
derived.rationale: AUDIT CORRECTION (phase C). Parts whose only support is their joint, declared with ctx.allow_isolated_part — which sdk_base.md sanctions verbatim for 'a joint-retained part intentionally disconnected by clearance', and which preflight permits (allow_overlap is not). The earlier draft kept the die parts OFF this list and promised them a rest-pose connection instead. That cannot hold: a die runs in a guide bore with the 1.1-1.2 mm radial clearance derived from 001, so it touches no other part at ANY pose, and find_unsupported_parts groups by physical contact at contact_tol=1e-6. Giving the ram cap a seated lap would only work at one end of its stroke and would drive the cap INTO the jaw beam at the other. The running fit is the source's own construction and must stay a gap; the joint is what carries the part, so allow_isolated_part is the correct and only honest declaration.

derived.name: lever_pivot_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: RUNNING FIT, stays a real gap. host_bore_r = member_bore_r + 0.0004, inverted. Source 001: lever bore 0.0068 (L150-L154) inside a frame bore 0.0072 (L99-L104). 001 is the ONLY record in the pool whose pivot needs no allowance; 002 runs the pin at exactly the lever bore (0.0055 = 0.0055) and 003 runs 0.2 mm of interference, and both pay for it with allow_overlap. So the fit is generalised from 001, not averaged over the pool.

derived.name: main_pivot_pin_r_m
derived.rationale: pin_r = bore_r - 0.0006. Source 001 L312: pin 0.0062 in a 0.0068 lever bore. Combined with the line above the pin clears the FRAME bore by 1.0 mm.

derived.name: pin_owner_part
derived.rationale: THE move that removes allow_overlap sites 5, 7, 8, 10 and 14. The pin visual belongs to the moving member, not the host (source 001 L311-L316 puts main_pivot_pin on moving_handle). Intra-part embedding is free (§1c), so the pin may sit in its own hub with zero clearance while only the host bore needs a real cross-part gap. 002 and 003 put the pin on the frame and needed an allowance for every single pivot.

derived.name: link_pin_r_m
derived.rationale: Same rule applied to the compound-link pins. Source 002 L291 and long_toggle_cheek L380 both build the pin equal to (or 0.05 mm larger than) the eye and declare an allowance; 0.6 mm makes it geometric.

derived.name: lever_standoff_m
derived.rationale: RUNNING FIT, stays a real gap. Lateral clearance between the lever plate and the frame cheek. The pool gives three solutions and all land on 1.0-1.25 mm: 001 offsets the handle visuals to y=-0.015 against a face at -0.010 (L293/L305, 1.0 mm); 003 seats the lever at y=+0.021 outboard of a +0.015 face (L308, 1.25 mm).

derived.name: lever_fork_slot_w_m
derived.rationale: The alternative stand-off: a forked handle root that straddles the frame. Source 002 L113-L119 cuts a 0.032 m slot for a 0.030 m frame -> 1.0 mm per side. Used when lever_plate_width_m >= frame_width_m.

derived.name: ram_guide_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: RUNNING FIT, stays a real gap — this is the one class §1c does NOT touch. guide_bore_r = shaft_r + 0.0012. Source 001 L108-L114: bore 0.0064 over a 0.0052 shaft. 002 makes both 0.0052 and declares allow_overlap (L498-L507); screw_press leaves 0.2 mm to its thread crests and does the same (L517-L527). 001's clearance is geometric, so it is the one generalised.

derived.name: anvil_guide_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: Same rule on the lower guide. Source 001 L115-L121: bore 0.0056 over a 0.0045 shank -> 1.1 mm.

derived.name: anvil_shaft_r_m
derived.rationale: Pool: 001 ram 0.0052 / anvil 0.0045; 002 ram 0.0052 / anvil 0.0047. The lower shank is consistently the slimmer of the two.

derived.name: max_die_step_r_m
derived.rationale: Hard ceiling on EVERY turned step of a die that passes through a guide bore, including the quick-change set collar and the screw thread crests. This is the single derivation that removes allow_overlap sites 6, 9, 11 and 13: the source let collars and crests exceed the bore they run in (003's r 0.0090 collar in a 0.0072 bore) and declared the interference away.

derived.name: set_collar_r_eff_m
derived.rationale: quick_change_yoke_clip only. Clamps 003's oversize collar below the receiver bore instead of nesting it inside the tube wall.

derived.name: ram_guide_depth_m
derived.rationale: Guide engagement. Source 002 L515-L523 asserts the ram stays >= 0.025 m inside the bore at every pose, so the bore must be at least the stroke plus that engagement. MECHANICAL_PRIORS §7: the opening is derived from the moving part's envelope, not from a magic constant.

derived.name: anvil_guide_depth_m
derived.rationale: Same rule on the anvil, whose travel is symmetric so the envelope is 2x.

derived.name: die_axis_x_m
derived.rationale: ONE station feeds BOTH die joints. Source 001 L379/L423 both use -0.102; 002 L363/L416 both use -0.124; compact_straight_head moves both to -0.065 and its author test L614-L625 asserts the two origins are equal to 1e-9. The category's defining assertion (expect_origin_distance axes='xy' max_dist=0.0005, 001 L611-L617) is only satisfiable if this is a single value.

derived.name: die_axis_y_m
derived.rationale: Both dies sit on the tool centre plane. 002 restates the coaxiality check INSIDE the anvil-adjusted pose (L678-L686), so adjustment may not break it either.

derived.name: upper_die_tip_offset_m
derived.rationale: Working face of the upper die below the squeeze datum.

derived.name: lower_die_tip_offset_m
derived.rationale: Working face of the lower die above the same datum, so the rest gap IS open_die_gap_m by construction rather than by coincidence.

derived.name: lower_die_parent_role
derived.rationale: The one relation that is candidate-scoped. Five mechanisms make both dies PRISMATIC children of the frame; direct_jaw_lever welds the lower set into the swinging jaw (L299-L306) because that is what an alligator squeezer is. Anchor `rivet_squeeze_direct_jaw_identity` covers this case so no legitimate candidate has to violate an anchor.

derived.name: die_retention_z_m
derived.rationale: Plane at which the retention scheme grips the set — a machined shoulder for three candidates, the horseshoe clip for the fourth.

derived.name: die_retention_r_m
derived.rationale: Radial extent of the retention seat, bounded by what fits through the guide bore.

derived.name: ram_travel_m
derived.rationale: THE derivation of the squeeze layer. Source 001: gap 0.0040, stroke 0.0040 (L385), residual ~0 with max_penetration 0.0002 asserted (L651-L660). Source 002: gap 0.0130, stroke 0.011 (L369), residual 0.0020 asserted 0.001..0.006 (L645-L654). The stroke is never a free constant.

derived.expression: screw_turn_range_rad / (2.0 * pi) * lead_m_per_turn if squeeze_mechanism == 'screw_press' else (cam_eccentricity_m * 2.0 if squeeze_mechanism == 'eccentric_cam' else ram_travel_m)
derived.name: ram_travel_available_m
derived.rationale: What the drive layer can actually deliver, checked against ram_travel_m. The screw gets turns x lead (source meta L379: 0.00175 m/turn over pi rad = 0.875 mm, which is why that candidate wants the smaller end of open_die_gap_m); the cam gets twice its eccentricity (L331: 0.0095 -> 0.019 m, ample). A mechanism that cannot reach the authored gap must widen its own range, not shrink the gap.

derived.name: throat_stroke_clearance_m
derived.rationale: Must stay > 0 for every frame x head_module pair. compact_straight_head has the tightest throat in the pool (0.032 m clear, from beams at z=360 and z=328), so this is where the constraint bites and it is a named corner.

derived.expression: upper_holder_h_m + die_tip_r_m * 2.0 if head_module == 'rotating_set_holder' else die_tip_r_m * 3.0
derived.name: upper_die_stack_h_m
derived.rationale: Axial height the upper die occupies inside the throat.

derived.expression: lower_holder_h_m + die_tip_r_m * 2.0 if head_module == 'rotating_set_holder' else die_tip_r_m * 3.0
derived.name: lower_die_stack_h_m
derived.rationale: Same for the lower die.

derived.name: upper_jaw_underside_z_m
derived.rationale: Where the frame's upper beam face has to sit so the die stack hangs below it.

derived.name: lower_jaw_top_z_m
derived.rationale: Mirror of the above for the lower beam.

derived.name: anvil_collar_counterbore_r_m
derived.rationale: allow_overlap site 3, removed. Source 002 L444-L463 declares the anvil collar 5.0-6.5 mm INSIDE the forged jaw and asserts a NEGATIVE gap of -0.0065..-0.0050. The rebuild cuts the counterbore the source implied, 0.5 mm oversize, so the collar seats in real material. All four 002-family mechanisms inherit this site.

derived.name: anvil_collar_counterbore_h_m
derived.rationale: Depth of that counterbore: the source's own declared penetration (6.5 mm) plus a 0.2 mm axial clearance so the seat is a real fit rather than a coincident face (fcl.collide reports distance 0 as a collision).

derived.name: screw_register_counterbore_r_m
derived.rationale: allow_overlap site 12, removed. Source screw_press L497-L516 seats the drive-head register with max_penetration 0.0035 instead of machining the pocket.

derived.name: screw_register_counterbore_h_m
derived.rationale: Depth plus the same 0.2 mm axial clearance.

derived.name: tommy_bushing_r_m
derived.rationale: allow_overlap site 14, removed. Source L563-L577 builds the bushing at exactly the bore radius (0.0042 = 0.0042); 001's 0.6 mm rule makes it a running fit.

derived.name: set_through_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: allow_overlap site 11, removed. alligator_jaw L749-L757 declares the set passing through the forged jaw tip; the rebuild cuts that through-bore 1.0 mm oversize.

derived.name: fixed_grip_root_x_m
derived.rationale: Where the fixed grip leaves the forging. The fixed grip is a VISUAL ON THE FRAME for 001 (L250-L260) and 003 (L177-L186) and their eight forks; only 002's family makes it a FIXED child part, which buys nothing kinematically and costs allow_overlap site 4. The rebuild welds it into the frame for every candidate.

derived.name: fixed_grip_len_m
derived.rationale: Grip length scaled to the travel it has to accommodate. Pool: 001's fixed grip spans z 41..151 mm = 0.110 m against 25 mm of travel.

derived.name: grip_travel_m
derived.rationale: Arc length the moving grip sweeps. Source 001 L661-L670 requires the grip centre to move MORE than 0.025 m; 002 L663 requires the lever end to rise more than 0.045 m; 003 L606-L614 more than 0.070 m.

derived.name: grip_lever_arm_m
derived.rationale: Distance from the pivot to the grip centre, derived so that the 25 mm minimum travel is met at whatever arc the mechanism authored. This is the pair-constraint the SourceMap flagged: lever length and lever travel cannot be sampled independently. direct_jaw_lever's 2 deg arc therefore forces a long jaw, which is exactly what its source builds (0.190 m, L274).

derived.name: closed_grip_gap_m
derived.rationale: Gap between the two grips at full lever travel. Source 001 L638-L647 asserts 0.001..0.005; 002 L664 asserts a 0.0005 minimum. Authored at the middle of the pool band so both bounds hold with margin, and re-derived rather than measured.

derived.name: moving_grip_stop_x_m
derived.rationale: Rest position of the moving grip, placed so that after grip_travel_m of closure the gap lands on closed_grip_gap_m. The handles never touch.

derived.name: grip_section_w_m
derived.rationale: Section width of a grip. Pool: 001 builds both grips at 0.027 m on a 0.020 m frame (L176, L208).

derived.name: reaction_bracket_required
derived.rationale: HOST ADAPTATION GATE. The eccentric cam is the only mechanism whose reaction load does not close through the frame's own throat: the lobe on the lever bears OUTWARD against a bracket, so the host must grow one. Source eccentric_cam L254-L284 builds a 6-point bracket with an r 0.007 reaction pin plus a Box(0.030,0.004,0.050) bridge. Without it the lobe presses on air and the record's own expect_contact at L556-L570 has nothing to hit. Encoded here rather than left in a comment so the adaptation is machine-visible.

derived.name: reaction_bracket_x_m
derived.rationale: Station of the reaction pin ahead of the pivot. Source L268 places it at x=0.058 with an r 0.007 pin, i.e. 8.3 pin radii, so it scales with the pin rather than being a magic constant.

derived.name: reaction_bracket_offset_y_m
derived.rationale: Lateral station of the bracket so the lobe reaches it with the same 1.0 mm stand-off every other cross-part pair uses. Source builds the lobe at y=-0.0245 (L333) and the bracket at y=-0.021 (L267).

derived.name: cam_bearing_clearance_m
derived.rationale: RUNNING FIT, stays a real gap. Radial gap between the lobe surface and the reaction pin at the open pose. The source asserts contact with contact_tol 0.0003 (L563-L570). AUDIT CORRECTION (phase C): a 0.2 mm gap does NOT connect the pair for fail_if_isolated_parts, whose contact_tol is 1e-6 — the earlier rationale was wrong about that. It must nonetheless stay a gap, because the lobe SWEEPS past the pin over the whole lever arc and any overlap would be a real interference at some sampled pose. The lever is carried by its own revolute and is declared with allow_isolated_part, which is what actually settles the support question.

derived.name: fixed_grip_is_separate_part
derived.rationale: RE-EXAMINED and corrected from the SourceMap. The SourceMap said the cam bracket blocks merging the FIXED fixed_handle into the frame. It does not: the bracket is FIXED to the frame either way, so merging it makes the bracket a frame feature and the lobe-to-bracket pair stays exactly as cross-part as before. What eccentric_cam actually needs is the derived bracket above, which is a local host adaptation. The merge is therefore unconditional for all six mechanisms, matching the majority construction (001, 003 and their eight forks) and removing allow_overlap site 4 outright.

derived.name: return_spring_pivot_xyz
derived.rationale: torsion_handle_spring wraps the tool's DRIVEN revolute axis. For five mechanisms that is the handle pivot at the origin (source L222-L223 hard-codes pivot_x=0, pivot_z=0.320, which is 001's pivot). screw_press has no handle pivot, but it does have a real revolute — the drive head about the squeeze axis (L287-L288) — so the coil moves there. Same construction, re-derived station, no candidate excluded.

derived.name: return_spring_standoff_m
derived.rationale: Clearance from the spring to the moving member. Source torsion_handle_spring: the coil spans y -0.0204..-0.0287 while the handle plate occupies -0.011..-0.019 -> 1.7 mm. The only cross-part spring clearance in the pool, so it is re-derived whenever the lever width changes rather than inherited as a constant.

derived.name: latch_parent_role
derived.rationale: 001 parents its wire hook to the MOVING handle (L453-L458); 003 parents its eye latch to the FRAME at the grip heel (L398-L403). Under screw_press there is no moving handle, so the hook falls back to 003's frame-heel construction. Local adaptation of an attested pattern, not an exclusion.

derived.name: latch_axle_r_m
derived.rationale: The pool's one allowance-free rotary capture: source 003 builds a 0.0022 eye bore over a 0.0020 axle and verifies it with expect_within (L546-L554). 0.2 mm is tighter than the 0.6 mm pin rule because the latch carries no load.

derived.name: latch_eye_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: wire_hook_latch has no annular eye in the source — its wire is simply speared by a pin 3 mm off the hinge axis, which is allow_overlap site 1. The rebuild gives it a real formed eye sized off its own wire, centred ON the joint origin, exactly as 003 does.

derived.name: latch_support_mode
derived.rationale: allow_overlap site 2 removed. 001 hooks the latch around the fixed grip with 1.4 mm of interference; 003's latch touches no host at all. The latch is carried by its hinge, which is what allow_isolated_part is for and what preflight permits.
